findings.assertion: A 1988 SEDUE/UAM-X bibliographic record states that the Convenio de Concertación Democrática for reconstruction housing was signed on 17 May 1986; its contents notes describe independent housing organizations, alternative designs and reviewed projects.
findings.source_locator: CID library catalog, 'Notas de contenido', p. title and description; original 1988 book and convenio not opened
findings.limitations: Date and project-characterization come from a library description, not a primary 1986 signed agreement. Do not infer actual individual signatories or compliance.

findings.assertion: The September 2000 Centro Histórico urban development program describes RHP replacement buildings as typically three levels, with sloped roofs, dwelling groups around patios or passageways, and 42 m² units with two bedrooms and a small kitchen/bath; facade design attempted to fit surrounding street proportions.
findings.source_locator: Gaceta Oficial DF 7 Sep 2000 no.153, printed p.62, housing section 'Conjuntos habitacionales de la reconstrucción', extracted lines 3829–3837
findings.limitations: Retrospective government typological description, not an individual measured building or guarantee all RHP blocks match. PDF page screenshots failed; machine text only.

findings.assertion: A 2000 official Centro Histórico program reports 48,800 RHP reconstructed dwellings in the broader program, while within the Centro Histórico perimeter it separately reports 796 expropriated properties, 13,562 dwellings and 1,271 accessory premises serving 67,410 residents; these categories have different denominators.
findings.source_locator: Gaceta Oficial DF 7 Sep 2000 no.153 printed p.63, extracted lines 3841–3850
findings.limitations: Retrospective totals reported by 2000 plan, not verified against original RHP final ledger; do not present property counts as housing-unit counts. Original PDF visual page inaccessible.

findings.assertion: The 2000 Centro Histórico program categorizes 370 RHP-treated properties as involving conservation interventions (172 wholly conserved, 35 retaining first bay, 64 facade preservation, 99 new-build projects with specific facade designs) and another 426 as demolished and wholly rebuilt.
findings.source_locator: Gaceta Oficial DF 7 Sep 2000 no.153 printed p.63, extracted lines 3846–3850
findings.limitations: Administrative classification according to a 2000 retrospective; verify categories, project definitions and original underlying 1998 source. Not a location-by-location survey.

findings.assertion: The 2000 Centro Histórico plan says INAH did not authorize proposed interventions in 95 out of 211 properties under consideration, citing high conservation costs or incompatible housing densities in several buildings; these were restrictions on a proposed subset, not a claim that 95 of all city properties were protected.
findings.source_locator: Gaceta Oficial DF 7 Sep 2000 no.153 printed p.63, extracted lines 3852–3867
findings.limitations: Retrospective official characterization, original INAH decisions and parcel lists unexamined. This is not proof that every excluded building survives today.

findings.assertion: An INAH journal abstract identifies Plaza de la Solidaridad near Alameda Central as occupying the former footprint of Hotel Regis and nearby destroyed commercial parcels; it dates the first commemorative tree at the then Jardín de la Solidaridad to 1986.
findings.source_locator: Sara Markowski (2004), INAH Antropología 75–76 pp.65–69, article abstract only
geographies: Plaza de la Solidaridad / Alameda Central
findings.limitations: Abstract only; article full text and historical maps not viewed. Current plaza layout, precise parcel boundaries, signage, and photo permissions not checked.
